title: Python OOP Revision Notes: Classes to ABCs
summary: Night-before revision of Python classes: instances vs class attributes, inheritance and MRO, super(), dunder methods, properties, dataclasses and abstract base classes, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Classes and the Object Mental Model
points: A class is a blueprint; calling it (Dog('Rex')) creates an instance, and classes are themselves objects (instances of type)
__init__(self, ...) initialises an already-created object (__new__ creates it); it must return None
self is just the first parameter, passed automatically: d.bark() is Dog.bark(d)
Instance attributes live in obj.__dict__; class attributes live in Class.__dict__ and are shared by all instances
Attribute lookup order: instance __dict__, then class, then base classes (via MRO), else AttributeError

chapters.title: Instance vs Class Attributes
points: Class attribute: defined in the class body, shared (Dog.species = 'canine'); instance attribute: set via self.x in __init__, per object
Reading d.species falls back to the class; assigning d.species = 'x' creates a new instance attribute that shadows the class one
Mutable class attribute trap: tags = [] in the class body is shared by every instance; create it in __init__ instead
Mutable default argument trap: def __init__(self, items=[]) shares one list across calls; use items=None then self.items = items or []
@classmethod receives cls (alternative constructors, e.g. from_json); @staticmethod receives nothing and is just a namespaced function

chapters.title: Inheritance, MRO and super()
points: class Child(Parent): inherits attributes and methods; override a method by redefining it; isinstance(c, Parent) is True
MRO is the method search order, computed by C3 linearisation; view it with Class.__mro__ or Class.mro()
Diamond: class D(B, C) with B and C both subclassing A gives MRO D, B, C, A, object, so A appears once and after both B and C
super() follows the MRO of type(self), not simply the parent class; so super().__init__() in cooperative multiple inheritance calls the next class in line
Forgetting super().__init__(...) in a subclass __init__ leaves parent attributes unset, giving AttributeError later

chapters.title: Dunder Methods and Properties
points: __repr__ is for developers (unambiguous, ideally eval-able) and __str__ for users; print falls back to __repr__ if __str__ is missing
__eq__ defines ==; defining __eq__ without __hash__ sets __hash__ to None, making instances unhashable
__len__, __getitem__, __iter__, __contains__ and __call__ make objects behave like containers or functions; __add__ and __lt__ overload operators
@property turns a method into read-only attribute access; add @x.setter for validation on assignment, with no () at the call site
Inside a property setter, store into a private name (self._x = v); assigning self.x = v there causes infinite recursion

chapters.title: Dataclasses and Abstract Base Classes
points: @dataclass auto-generates __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ from annotated fields: @dataclass class P: x: int; y: int = 0
Mutable defaults are rejected (tags: list = [] raises ValueError); use field(default_factory=list)
Options: frozen=True makes instances immutable and hashable, order=True adds comparisons, __post_init__ runs after the generated __init__
Fields with defaults must come after fields without defaults, otherwise TypeError
ABC with @abstractmethod: class Shape(ABC) cannot be instantiated until a subclass overrides every abstract method, otherwise TypeError at instantiation
ABC vs plain base class: ABC enforces the interface at instantiation, whereas a plain base class only raises NotImplementedError when the method is called

chapters.title: Python OOP Cheat Sheet
points: Create and init: obj = C(args) calls __new__ then __init__; self.x = v sets instance state
Lookup: instance, class, then MRO; inspect with vars(obj), C.__mro__, dir(obj)
Method kinds: instance method (self), @classmethod (cls), @staticmethod (neither)
Properties and dunders: @property/@x.setter, __repr__, __eq__ with __hash__, __len__, __iter__
Dataclass and ABC one-liners: @dataclass(frozen=True, order=True), field(default_factory=list), class A(ABC) with @abstractmethod
